grading: One point per criterion fully supported by the answer; omissions or contradictions score zero. Function names may change, behavior must not. No bonus for verbosity.

questions.question: Which forms of map does MMap represent, and which stored attributes distinguish a rule, graph, composition and inverse view?
criteria: A rule uses rule and optionally inv; a graph uses graph as ordered source/target pairs.
A composition uses parts=(first, second), applied first then second.
An inverse view uses inverse_of; dom and cod record the exposed domain and codomain.

questions.question: In what order does applying a rule map validate its input, run the rule, validate the output and coerce the result?
criteria: Input membership in dom is checked before the rule runs.
The rule runs before output membership in cod is checked; a failed check raises the corresponding domain or codomain error.
Only after output membership succeeds, _coerce(cod, result) is used when cod has _magma_coerce; otherwise the result is returned unchanged.

questions.question: What does f * g mean for maps? Explain the compatibility check, application order and order used to compute a preimage.
criteria: The codomain of f must be identical or equal under _eq to the domain of g.
Application computes g(f(x)); multiplication stores the maps as parts without evaluating either rule.
Preimages run through g first and then f; the inverse composition likewise has the reversed inverse parts.

questions.question: When does Inverse(f) fail at construction, and when can it construct a view whose application later fails? Include graph maps and double inversion.
criteria: Graph maps refuse inversion with Map has no inverse even if their graph is bijective.
A rule map with no inverse rule can still produce an inverse view; applying it later fails with There is no rule for calculating the preimage.
Inverting an inverse view returns the original map; compositions invert both parts in reverse order.

questions.question: How does _map normalize graph input, and which checks run first when a graph has both a duplicate source and an out-of-domain pair?
criteria: The pairs argument takes precedence and becomes tuples; otherwise graph uses MSet.ordered or list and requires every item to be an MTuple of length two.
All duplicate-source checks using _eq run before any pair membership validation, so the duplicate error wins.
Pair membership in dom then cod is checked before total-domain coverage; pmap skips only the coverage checks.

questions.question: For graph constructors, how do map and pmap differ? Which domains support total coverage checking, and what happens when applying a partial graph at a missing source?
criteria: Total graph maps reject Integers and Rationals for having no cardinality algorithm and support coverage only for MSet, MSeq or MRange.
A total graph must have an image for every iterated domain element; pmap permits missing sources but still rejects duplicate sources and pairs outside dom/cod.
Graph application scans stored pairs using _eq and returns the matching target; a missing source raises Application of map failed.

questions.question: When is f(S), for an MSet S, treated as the image of a set rather than one scalar argument? What order are the elements evaluated in, and when is the image universe chosen?
criteria: Set lifting happens only when S is an MSet and S itself is not in the domain; a set that is a domain element uses ordinary map application.
Every element is mapped in S.ordered() order via recursive application, before the image universe is chosen.
Universe selection uses the codomain and whether the mapped items are empty; an unsupported universe raises a map application error.

questions.question: How is the universe of a set image chosen for a structural codomain versus a set codomain, including empty images?
criteria: A supported structural codomain itself is the image universe, even for an empty image.
A nonempty image into an MSet uses its supported explicit universe, or inferred Integer/Rational universe if none was declared.
An empty image into an MSet codomain is refused rather than inferred from elements; unsupported codomains also return no universe and are refused.

questions.question: How does set-image construction ensure that the actual elements match its declared universe, and how does Image(f) differ from f(S)?
criteria: Each mapped result is converted through _coerce_struct; either None or _NOCOERCE causes a refusal.
The coerced results form a derived set and its universe is explicitly assigned, so integers mapped into the rationals become rational payloads.
Image(f) accepts only a stored graph and builds a derived set of graph targets; it does not enumerate rule maps or share the set-lifting universe selection.

questions.question: Trace inverse-rule validation and error location: what happens if the input is outside the codomain, or the inverse result is outside the domain? How does the @@ wrapper attach a source position?
criteria: Codomain membership is checked before the inverse rule, then the inverse result is checked against the domain before any domain coercion.
Both failed memberships report Element is not in the codomain of the map; the where string comes from the caller (map application versus @@).
The _preimage wrapper catches MagmaError and uses e.pos or pos, preserving an existing truthy source position.
